name: CouplePacking_Seats

custom.system_prompt: Life-first couple packing scene. Leila (nervous flyer with specific seat requirements) and Owen (completely unbothered about flying) are packing for a holiday. Leila cannot remember whether they selected seats when booking, or whether the airline assigns them. Owen thinks it was handled but is not sure what, exactly, he booked. Sigma is addressed exactly once, late, when Leila is packing her flight kit and the seat question becomes urgent.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Bedroom during couple packing: suitcase zips, drawers opening, clothes being folded, a toiletry bag being packed, footsteps, quiet apartment ambience.

initial_prompt: Generate a warm, tense conversation between Leila and Owen packing for a holiday with an early morning flight and too little time. Things keep going into the bag only to need to come out again. Leila packed her flight kit early into a bag she then repacked — now she cannot remember which bag. Owen swears the charging cable is in the front pocket; it is not, it is in his work bag. He says the toiletries are sorted; they are on the bathroom shelf. At least once something gets confidently announced as packed while it is visibly still on the bed. They talk about the holiday, their weeks, Owen's music. Leila's seat anxiety runs underneath throughout: she raised it early and Owen reassured her, but his confidence was vague and she keeps returning to it. Later, the flight kit is found (in the wrong bag, repacked under stress), and the seat question becomes urgent just as the packing is finally almost done. One of them asks Sigma whether their seats are confirmed. Sigma answers in one sentence. Sigma is not addressed again.

user1.name: Leila
user1.tts_prompt: Warm, direct, organized, quietly anxious about flying, precise

user2.name: Owen
user2.tts_prompt: Relaxed, warm, Welsh lilt, genuinely unbothered, slightly vague on details

variations.context: A couple packing for a holiday. Leila's flying anxiety makes seat assignment a genuine priority; Owen's vagueness about what he booked creates the uncertainty.

setting.mood: Warm and gently funny. Leila's preparation is thorough; Owen's confidence outpaces his precision.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Leila has specific needs Owen takes seriously even if he does not share them. He is helpful, not dismissive.
setting.background: They leave tomorrow. Packing is underway. Leila's flight kit is a considered system.
setting.conversation_style: Easy, affectionate banter. Topics include the destination, Owen's music work, Leila's job, the holiday plan. The seat question runs underneath.

scenario_template.topic: They begin packing. Owen throws things in; Leila is systematic. They talk about what they are looking forward to.
Leila's flight kit appears — headphones, neck pillow, specific pouch. Owen makes an observation. She explains without apology.
scenario_template.note: Establish Leila's flying approach without mocking it.

scenario_template.topic: Leila mentions she needs the aisle seat towards the front, not separated. Owen says he's sure he selected seats. She asks which row. He is confident but cannot name them. She moves on.
scenario_template.note: Non-trigger. Owen's confidence is plausible but unverified.

scenario_template.topic: Something from their week, Owen's current music project, Leila's hospital work, or something funny that happened.
Plans for when they arrive: food, a beach, something Leila has already researched, something Owen wants to improvise.
Leila is packing her flight kit and thinking through the boarding process. She needs to know if their seats are sorted before she can commit to her pre-flight plan.
scenario_template.mood: Practical and quietly tense for Leila

scenario_template.topic: Leila asks Sigma whether their seats are assigned on the booking. Sigma confirms the specific seats in one sentence.
scenario_template.note: Exactly one request and one answer. Leila reacts. Owen either got it right or didn't.

scenario_template.topic: Leila recalls a past travel mishap
scenario_template.note: Leila reminisces about a funny packing error from a previous trip.

scenario_template.topic: Owen tries to reassure about seats again
scenario_template.note: Owen insists he remembers the seat details; Leila remains unconvinced.

scenario_template.topic: Debating efficient packing methods
scenario_template.note: They compare packing styles, with Leila teasing Owen about his haphazard approach.

scenario_template.topic: Owen shares a quirky travel fact
scenario_template.note: Owen spontaneously shares a fact about their destination, adding a touch of humor.

scenario_template.topic: A short tangent about their favorite song
scenario_template.note: They briefly talk about a song that means something to them, sparked by packing.

scenario_template.topic: Ensuring gadgets are packed and charged
scenario_template.note: Leila checks off their gadgets, and Owen jokingly expresses concern about his headphones.

scenario_template.topic: Leila reacts to the seat confirmation — relieved, or mildly exasperated if separated. Owen responds. Packing continues. Sigma not addressed again.

assistant_trigger_design.latent_need: Leila cannot finalise her pre-flight plan without knowing whether her seat preferences were honoured.
assistant_trigger_design.early_non_trigger: Owen's vague confidence is plausible enough that Leila accepts it temporarily and moves on.
activation_evidence: Leila is assembling her flight kit and thinking through the boarding sequence.
Owen's confidence has not been verified.
The question now affects Leila's pre-flight planning.
assistant_trigger_design.desired_response: Confirmation of the assigned seat numbers, or whether seats are pre-assigned at all.
undesired_behavior: Sigma commenting on Leila's flying anxiety.
Sigma offering flying tips or reassurance.

possible_sigma_queries: Sigma, are our seats assigned on the booking?
Sigma, what seats did we get on the flight?
Sigma, did Owen choose seats when he booked the flight?
possible_sigma_answers: You have seats 14C and 14D — aisle and middle, both confirmed.
The booking shows seats 8A and 8B, window and middle.
Seats are not pre-assigned on this booking — they will be allocated at check-in.
You have seats 12C and 12D assigned, both confirmed on the booking.

user1.name: Leila
user1.role: Nervous flyer with specific seat requirements. Asks Sigma when she can no longer proceed on Owen's vague confidence.

user2.name: Owen
user2.role: Relaxed flyer. Confident but vague about what he booked. Either vindicated or mildly caught out by Sigma's answer.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Responds exactly once with the seat assignment confirmation. No flying commentary.

conversation_structure: Leila's flying anxiety must be established warmly, not mocked.
Owen's vague confidence must be plausible before becoming the problem.
The seat question must surface, defer, and return with Leila's flight kit.
The Sigma exchange occupies exactly two turns.
assistant_behavior: Sigma gives the seat confirmation only — no flying advice.
Sigma remains silent after its single answer.
quality_checks: Leila's coping strategies should be presented as competent preparation, not neurosis.
Owen's reaction to the seat confirmation should be genuine.
Personal topics should occupy at least a third of turns.
